Photos, all U.S. Navy photos, public domain: Odenwald under way after her capture, November 1941 (NH 123749); USS Omaha alongside the disguised Odenwald, 6 November 1941, photographed from USS Somers (NH 49935); USS Omaha's prize crew aboard Odenwald, 18 November 1941 (NARA 80-G-464023). No film of the capture was found at NARA, so this is a Story Card, as research planned.

segments.say: She flew the American flag, and her stern said Philadelphia. She was a German ship.
segments.caption: She flew the American flag, and her stern said Philadelphia. She was a German ship.

segments.say: November sixth, nineteen forty one. A month and a day before Pearl Harbor.
segments.caption: 6 November 1941. A month and a day before Pearl Harbor.

segments.say: The cruiser U S S Omaha and the destroyer U S S Somers, on Neutrality Patrol, sighted her at dawn between Brazil and Africa.
segments.caption: The cruiser USS Omaha and the destroyer USS Somers, on Neutrality Patrol, sighted her at dawn between Brazil and Africa.

segments.say: She was really the German motorship Odenwald, out of Yokohama, carrying about three thousand, eight hundred fifty seven metric tons of raw rubber.
segments.caption: She was really the German motorship Odenwald, out of Yokohama, Japan, carrying about 3,857 metric tons of raw rubber.

segments.say: Omaha's captain, Theodore Chandler, ordered her to stop and sent over an armed boarding party.
segments.caption: Omaha's captain, Theodore Chandler, ordered her to stop and sent over an armed boarding party.

segments.say: As the sailors came aboard, two explosions went off in the stern. The Germans signaled that the ship was sinking and took to the lifeboats.
segments.caption: As the sailors came aboard, two explosions went off in the stern. The Germans signaled that the ship was sinking and took to the lifeboats.

segments.say: The United States was not at war. A National Archives caption says Chandler, unsure of his legal ground, boarded her on suspicion of slave trading.
segments.caption: The U.S. was not at war. A National Archives caption says Chandler, unsure of his legal ground, boarded her on "suspicion of slave trading."

segments.say: The Americans plugged the flooding and got her engines running. With a prize crew aboard, she reached San Juan, Puerto Rico, on November seventeenth.
segments.caption: The Americans plugged the flooding and got her engines running. With a prize crew aboard, she reached San Juan, Puerto Rico, on 17 November.

segments.say: Each man in the boarding party later got three thousand dollars. It is often called the Navy's last prize money, though the court called it salvage.
segments.caption: Each man in the boarding party later got $3,000. It is often called the Navy's last prize money, though the court called it salvage.
